notes: Cross-sectional survey of 110 smallholder dairy farmers, Njoro Sub-County, Nakuru, Kenya; multivariate probit of adoption of nine CSTs on 12 socio-economic/institutional variables (Table 4). Extracted coefficients for the in-scope columns only: improved fodder, silage and hay, zero grazing (feed_mgmt) and agroforestry (trees_in_farmlands); every coefficient extracted, significant or not. Not extracted: rainwater harvesting (water_harvesting, out_of_scope; tagged but recorded only), biogas, improved livestock, solar energy, drought-resistant crops (not defined practices), and constants. No adoption rates are reported anywhere in the paper (rates are in a companion paper, ref. 36). Survey year not stated (NACOSTI ref /P/25/ hints 2025, not used). Adoption window 'at least once during a production cycle' coded ever_vs_current unstated. Inconsistency: abstract says household size significantly reduced adoption of 'improved fodder', Table 4 and the text show it is improved livestock (-0.151**); improved fodder coefficient 0.105 not significant - table taken. Text says road status significant at 10% for hay and silage (matches table *) and 1% for agroforestry (matches ***). Variable coding (which category = 1) is not given for most variables.
